version.changelog: mcp --expose read / --allow-write: offer only read tools plus chosen write tools

llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed, read-only VMware log-query integration, but users should treat its log access and local credential file as sensitive.

dimensions.detail: Network use is described as calls to the configured Log Insight appliance, TLS verification defaults on, and no webhook or unrelated outbound data flow is described.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is via the disclosed uv package vmware-log-insight==2.1.0 with Bash allowed for CLI/MCP setup. The artifact does not bundle executable scripts in the inspected workspace, but the installed package itself was not present for code review.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Usage is scoped to VMware/vSphere/ESXi Log Insight contexts, includes routing away from unrelated VMware tasks, bounds searches by time/limits, and explicitly treats returned log text as untrusted data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill creates normal local configuration and credential files under ~/.vmware-log-insight and records audit entries under ~/.vmware/audit.db. This is disclosed and purpose-aligned, but the .env credential storage is persistent and only obfuscated, not encrypted.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is VMware Log Insight search, aggregation, metadata, and alert-history reads; the artifact repeatedly states seven read-only tools and no ingest, create, edit, or delete capability. Centralized logs can contain sensitive operational data, so least-privilege Log Insight accounts matter.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you need an agent to read VMware Log Insight data. Use a read-only Log Insight service account, prefer injecting the password from a secret manager instead of storing it in .env, keep TLS verification enabled outside labs, and remember that returned logs may contain sensitive or attacker-controlled text.
llm.findings:
[PE3] expected: Credential handling is real: the setup uses VMWARE_LOG_INSIGHT_<TARGET>_PASSWORD and supports ~/.vmware-log-insight/.env. The artifact discloses chmod 600, warns that b64 is obfuscation rather than encryption, and recommends secret-manager injection for real at-rest secrecy, so this is a purpose-aligned risk rather than evidence of theft.
[TM1] expected: The --skip-auth flag appears only on the doctor diagnostic command. The artifact does not show it enabling unauthenticated log reads or bypassing the MCP tools.
[TM3] expected: The same --skip-auth diagnostic option is disclosed; TLS verification is stated to be on by default, and the query defaults are bounded rather than unbounded.
[RA2] expected: The cited configuration directory and audit database are disclosed local state for setup and audit logging, not cron jobs, startup hooks, services, or hidden background persistence.
[PE2] expected: The cited chmod 600 command changes file permissions for the local .env file and does not request sudo or root execution.
